exposure: Being approached for delivery room studies
Consent process for delivery room studies
outcome: Parental experiences with consent for delivery room studies
Parental perceptions of consent for delivery room studies
Parental understanding of delivery room studies
cohort: The study participants were 25 parents of very and extreme preterm infants.
finding: Most parents found being approached for delivery room studies valuable due to appropriate timing, communication, and compassion, despite the stressful situation, though parental misunderstanding of study aims, randomization, and risk was common, and there was no consensus on deferred consent for all studies, but it was considered appropriate for observational studies.
